name: smwgraphics-bomberman-ii-intro-cutscene
title: Bomberman II - Intro Cutscene
description:
The city seen in the opening sequence of Bomberman II for the NES.

Includes a church cross that was removed from the international releases, due to Nintendo's censorship back then. Thanks to NES Boy216 for telling me about this.

There's four palettes included:
- FCEUX colors;
- FCEUX, but with a lighter outline;
- NES colors;
- NES colors but with a lighter outline;

Pick the one you like the most. Personally, I think that the ones with lighter outlines work the best with SMW style.

The colors and outline are easy enough to edit. If you want to remove the cross, for some reason, delete the last two 8x8 tiles in the provided bin file.

A good fit for retro themed town levels.

versions.title: Bomberman II - Intro Cutscene

name: smwgraphics-snow-bros-arcade-world
title: Snow Bros. (Arcade) - World 2
description:
Ah yes, the bright and colorful yet sort of "abstract" world that I can't figure out if it's some sort of carnival or a Krtek-style toy factory (for who doesn't know about Krtek aka The Little Mole, it was an old Czechoslovakian animated series that was usually quite wholesome and cutesy compared to the creepy or scary animations that we know Czechoslovakia for nowadays, including Fantastic Planet, if I remember correctly. There was a scene in a Krtek short about Krtek and his friends going to find shelter in the city after the forest they called home was deforestated, but let's get straight to the point now, Krtek and his friends become famous and enter a colorful toy factory where they started making Krtek dolls. Anyways, if you didn't know, you can find Krtek and his friends literally EVERYWHERE around Prague, but let's move on, shall we?)
I couldn't find any tiles in the original game's files that made the scaffoldings cross between each other or something, so I edited the Map16 to make them connect properly without making them look too "choppy", without risking of having more cutoff, not to mention that I've added 2 custom-made tiles specifically to complete this tileset

name: smwgraphics-super-mario-world-styled-luigi-beta-sma2-inspired
title: Super Mario World Styled Luigi (Beta & SMA2-inspired)
description:
This started out as an opposite to QuadFactor's SMA2 Mario, to "de-advance-ify" SMA2 Luigi, but I decided to shift the scope to create a Luigi that feels like he came out of base game back in the 1990s. Mainly based off of the 1989 beta and SMA2 Luigi but takes some notes from SMAS/SMM2 and SMB3 Luigi.



Includes:

- GFX32 and PlayerGFX for 32x32 compat (with SMAS poses)

- Same as above with but without vanilla inaccuracies

- GFX00 (and a corrected version), 10 (one for the 32x32 patch too), 22, and 24

- GFX 28 to swap nametags

- SMW palette (vanilla), SMA2 palette (blue overalls), and SMM2 palette (Mario's skin tone) for Luigi as Player 1

- OW palettes for adjusted Yoshi colors and Luigi as Player 1 (has both blue and purple overalls)


I recommend you use them with patches that fix tile errors in the vanilla game (specifically the first cape flight frame and small victory pose while riding Yoshi)

The GFX32 files have a small p-speed jump frame in an unused tile.

Feel free to edit if you want to mix and match the jank and corrected sprites or if you need compat with custom items/outfits

versions.title: Super Mario World Styled Luigi (Beta & SMA2-inspired)
